"""Pre-render script: remove '### Due Date' headings and the date line that follows."""
import re
import glob

pattern = re.compile(r'### Due Date\n\n?[^\n]+\n?')

for filepath in glob.glob('**/*.qmd', recursive=True):
    with open(filepath, 'r') as f:
        original = f.read()
    cleaned = pattern.sub('', original)
    if cleaned != original:
        with open(filepath, 'w') as f:
            f.write(cleaned)
        print(f"Stripped Due Date from {filepath}")

Content lives in bleds22e/DataWrangling (GitHub). The website repo (DataWranglingWebsite) is config-only. CI/CD fetches the DataWrangling content, runs `quarto render`, and deploys.

**Design decisions:**
- `code-tools: source: true` — adds a "</> Code" download button for .qmd source on every lesson/assignment page
- `strip_due_date.R` as a `pre-render` script — removes `### Due Date` heading + following date line from .qmd files before rendering, so Due Date is absent from both the website and downloaded source files
- `_print-button.html` via `include-after-body` — fixed "Save as PDF" button using `window.print()`; hidden on home page via JS path check; hidden from print output via `@media print` CSS
- Sidebar `collapse-level: 1` — sidebar sections collapsed by default; Quarto auto-expands the active section
- Home page topics are linked to the first lesson in each sidebar section

**Why:** Assignment Due Dates make sense in the teaching repo but not on the public website. The pre-render R script (not Python, not Lua filter) was chosen at user preference.

name: Build and Deploy Website

on:
  repository_dispatch:
    types: [datawrangling-updated]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      semester:
        description: 'Semester tag for snapshot release (e.g., spring-2025). Leave empty for a regular build.'
        required: false
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: write
  pages: write
  id-token: write

jobs:
  build-deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      DATAWRANGLING_SHA: ${{ github.event.client_payload.sha || github.sha }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout DataWranglingWebsite
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Checkout DataWrangling
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: bleds22e/DataWrangling
          token: ${{ secrets.DATAWRANGLING_PAT }}
          path: datawrangling

      - name: Copy course files from DataWrangling
        run: |
          # Copy only the .qmd files needed for the website
          find datawrangling/Week*/ \( \
            -name "*_Instructor.qmd" \
            -o -name "*_Assignment.qmd" \
            -o -name "*_Assignment_AnswerKey.qmd" \
            -o -name "*_Assignment_key.qmd" \
            -o -name "filepaths.qmd" \
            -o -name "Week10_VersionControl.qmd" \
          \) | while IFS= read -r f; do
            rel="${f#datawrangling/}"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$rel")"
            cp "$f" "$rel"
          done
          # Copy all data and image assets
          find datawrangling/Week*/ \( \
            -name "*.csv" -o -name "*.txt" \
            -o -name "*.png" -o -name "*.jpg" -o -name "*.jpeg" \
            -o -name "*.tif" -o -name "*.tiff" \
            -o -name "*.shp" -o -name "*.dbf" -o -name "*.prj" -o -name "*.shx" \
            -o -name "*.R" \
          \) | while IFS= read -r f; do
            rel="${f#datawrangling/}"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$rel")"
            cp "$f" "$rel"
          done
          cp -r datawrangling/PeerCodeReview . 2>/dev/null || true
          rm -rf datawrangling

      - name: Patch qmd files (strip format, add eval:false to assignments)
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
          import re, glob

          yaml_pattern = re.compile(r'^(---\n)(.*?)(---)', re.DOTALL)

          # Strip 'format:' from all qmd files so they inherit HTML from _quarto.yml
          for path in glob.glob('**/*.qmd', recursive=True):
              if path == 'index.qmd':
                  continue
              text = open(path).read()
              def strip_format(m):
                  header = re.sub(r'^format:.*\n', '', m.group(2), flags=re.MULTILINE)
                  return m.group(1) + header + m.group(3)
              patched = yaml_pattern.sub(strip_format, text, count=1)
              if patched != text:
                  open(path, 'w').write(patched)
                  print(f'Stripped format: {path}')

          # Add eval:false to assignment scaffold files
          for path in glob.glob('**/Week*_Assignment.qmd', recursive=True):
              if 'AnswerKey' in path or '_key' in path:
                  continue
              text = open(path).read()
              def inject(m):
                  header = m.group(2)
                  if 'eval: false' in header:
                      return m.group(0)
                  return m.group(1) + header + 'execute:\n  eval: false\n' + m.group(3)
              patched = yaml_pattern.sub(inject, text, count=1)
              if patched != text:
                  open(path, 'w').write(patched)
                  print(f'Patched eval:false: {path}')
          PYEOF

      - name: Install libcurl system dependency
        run: sudo apt-get install -y libcurl4-openssl-dev

      - name: Set up R
        uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
        with:
          r-version: 'release'
          use-public-rspm: true

      - name: Cache R packages
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ env.R_LIBS_USER }}
          key: r-pkgs-v5
          restore-keys: r-pkgs-

      - name: Install R packages
        run: |
          Rscript -e 'install.packages("pak", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")'
          Rscript -e 'pak::pak(c(
            "tidyverse", "terra", "lterdatasampler", "portalr",
            "palmerpenguins", "usethis", "knitr", "rmarkdown"
          ))'

      - name: Set up Quarto
        uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/setup@v2

      - name: Render website
        run: quarto render --to html

      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/publish@v2
        with:
          target: gh-pages
          render: false

      - name: Create semester release
        if: ${{ github.event.inputs.semester != '' }}
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          tag_name: ${{ github.event.inputs.semester }}
          name: ${{ github.event.inputs.semester }}
          body: |
            Website snapshot for **${{ github.event.inputs.semester }}**.

            Built from DataWrangling commit: `${{ env.DATAWRANGLING_SHA }}`

            View the live site: https://bleds22e.github.io/DataWranglingWebsite/

Now here's what you need to add to `.github/workflows/trigger-website.yml` in the **DataWrangling** repo:

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags:
      - 'spring-*'
      - 'fall-*'
      - 'summer-*'
```

And update the `client-payload` line to include the tag name:

```yaml
client-payload: '{"sha": "${{ github.sha }}", "ref": "${{ github.ref }}", "semester": "${{ startsWith(github.ref, ''refs/tags/'') && github.ref_name || '' }}"}'
```

So the full workflow in DataWrangling would look like:

```yaml
name: Trigger Website Build

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags:
      - 'spring-*'
      - 'fall-*'
      - 'summer-*'

jobs:
  trigger:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: peter-evans/repository-dispatch@v3
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.WEBSITE_DISPATCH_TOKEN }}
          repository: bleds22e/DataWranglingWebsite
          event-type: datawrangling-updated
          client-payload: '{"sha": "${{ github.sha }}", "ref": "${{ github.ref }}", "semester": "${{ startsWith(github.ref, ''refs/tags/'') && github.ref_name || '' }}"}'
```

Then to cut a semester release, you'd just:
```bash
git tag spring-2025
git push origin spring-2025
```
